title: Market update - November 27th, 2026
summary: Bitcoin recovered towards US$61k after dipping below US$58k, as oversold readings meet a hawkish Fed. Read our analysis of the AI leverage link and why the lower end of the range looks attractive.
body_markdown:
## Bitcoin holds near US$61k as oversold readings meet a hawkish Fed


After briefly falling below US$58k on a slightly hotter core PCE print, Bitcoin recovered towards US$61k even as US technology stocks came under renewed pressure. The Nasdaq was hit particularly hard by weakness in AI and semiconductors, although much of the damage was recovered before the close. What stands out is that Bitcoin has shown relative resilience through this latest period of stress rather than simply following tech lower tick for tick. That does not make a bottom certain, but it does suggest a fair amount of forced selling has already taken place.


### Backward-looking data, falling oil


The dollar index (DXY) is now close to its highest in about 19 months, which is hardly helpful, yet Treasury yields have started to retreat from their recent highs after briefly moving above 5%, suggesting increasing risk aversion rather than a straightforward repricing of rates. Personal income was stronger than expected and core PCE was slightly above expectations year on year,¹ so the Fed still has enough inflation in the data to remain cautious. The problem is that the data is backward-looking. Oil has fallen from roughly US$113 in late October to around US$97 per barrel, with the impact of the move taking time to transmit through to headline inflation. Earlier in the year, the rise in oil following the Iran escalation took several quarters to filter through. The same lag should work in reverse, which leaves the Fed at risk of staying too hawkish just as some of the underlying pressure is beginning to fade.


### AI leverage is the link to Bitcoin


Markets had at one stage over the last few weeks priced around 29 basis points of tightening for December, effectively assigning some probability to a move larger than 25bp, but that has started to unwind despite the firmer inflation data. The damage being done by tighter financial conditions is becoming more visible, particularly in technology. The AI trade remains highly sensitive to rates because so much of it is built around high growth expectations, leverage and increasingly complex financing structures. If expected returns begin to disappoint, leverage could turn a valuation correction into a liquidity event (a forced sale of assets to meet debts) surprisingly quickly. Bitcoin is not fundamentally tied to that story, but in the short term both assets draw from the same pool of risk-sensitive capital, so stress in one can easily spill into the other.


### Oversold, and approaching past cycle lows


What makes the current setup more interesting is how stretched the market has become. Daily RSI (a momentum gauge where readings below 30 mark oversold conditions) recently fell to around 17, close to the levels seen around the 2022 trough and among the most oversold readings in Bitcoin’s history. It is not a particularly useful indicator in the middle of a trend, but historically it has been much better at identifying exhaustion at extreme price highs or lows. Price relative to realised value (MVRV) is also highlighting that Bitcoin is approaching valuation levels associated with the major lows of 2015, 2019 and 2022. We are not quite at those extremes, but for an investor looking one or two years ahead the valuation is becoming increasingly attractive.


### A slow bottom, not a V


That still does not make the next few weeks straightforward. Dealers are cutting exposure, year-end liquidity is likely to thin and weaker order books can exaggerate relatively modest flows in either direction. A slow bottoming process looks more plausible than a clean V-shaped recovery, particularly while the AI trade remains unstable and the Fed is still leaning hawkish. Our base case remains that Bitcoin trades broadly between US$60k and US$90k until there is a more meaningful change in liquidity or monetary policy. With sentiment close to capitulation, positioning heavily reduced and valuations approaching levels normally associated with major troughs, the lower end of that range is beginning to look considerably more attractive for investors with a longer time horizon.


### Sources


1 US Bureau of Economic Analysis, Personal Income and Outlays, October 2026, 25 Nov 2026: core PCE up 3.3% year on year, personal income up 0.7%. Consensus of 3.2% and 0.4%: LSEG survey, 25 Nov 2026
